newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes fall with WTI, dealing idle.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes fall with WTI, dealing idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell with weaker West Texas Intermediate (WTI) markets, but traders continued to avoid fixed deals for Alaska North Slope (ANS).
Outright prices for WTI fell to $24.80/24.90 a barrel, pressured by profit-taking on NYMEX, which saw November crude fall as much as 71 cents to $24.71.

Bearish sentiment continued among buyers, who saw inventories flush in PADD 5. Stocks stood 3.6 million over year-ago levels, at 68.4 million, according to inventory data released Tueday from the American Petroleum Institute.
Few ANS deals were expected this week, with a industry function running between now and Monday.
Traders said margins remained weak, as product prices out West lagged the recent rallies in crude.
Outright prices for ANS eased to $22.40/22.70, with deltas steady at $2.30 less November WTI.
ANS Buyers bid around $2.50 under November WTI, while a major producer continued to offer at $2.10.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
California heavy crudes remained flat. Kern River crude was $17.30/17.50 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington crude stayed $18.65/18.75 a barrel.
